{{Short description|Invariant of vertex algebra}}
{{Technical|date=January 2024}}
In mathematics, the '''Zhu algebra''' and the closely related '''C<sub>2</sub>-algebra''', introduced by Yongchang Zhu in his PhD thesis, are two [[associative algebra|associative algebras]] canonically constructed from a given [[vertex operator algebra]].<ref name=":0" /> Many important [[representation theory|representation theoretic]] properties of the vertex algebra are logically related to properties of its Zhu algebra or C<sub>2</sub>-algebra.

==Definitions==
Let <math>V = \bigoplus_{n \ge 0} V_{(n)}</math> be a graded [[vertex operator algebra]] with <math>V_{(0)} = \mathbb{C}\mathbf{1}</math> and let <math>Y(a, z) = \sum_{n \in \Z} a_n z^{-n-1}</math> be the vertex operator associated to <math>a \in V</math>. Define <math>C_2(V)\subset V</math> to be the subspace spanned by elements of the form <math>a_{-2} b</math> for <math>a,b \in V</math>. An element <math>a \in V</math> is homogeneous with <math>\operatorname{wt} a = n</math> if <math>a \in V_{(n)}</math>. There are two [[Binary operation|binary operations]] on <math>V</math> defined by <math display="block">a * b = \sum_{i \ge 0} \binom{\operatorname{wt} a}{i} a_{i-1}b</math>, <math display="block">a \circ b = \sum_{i \ge 0} \binom{\operatorname{wt}a}{i} a_{i-2} b</math> for homogeneous elements and extended linearly to all of <math>V</math>. Define <math>O(V)\subset V</math> to be the span of all elements <math>a\circ b</math>.

The algebra <math>A(V) := V/O(V)</math> with the binary operation induced by <math>*</math> is an associative algebra called the ''Zhu algebra'' of <math>V</math> <ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Zhu |first=Yongchang |date=1996 |title=Modular invariance of characters of vertex operator algebras |journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society |volume=9 |issue=1 |pages=237–302 |doi=10.1090/s0894-0347-96-00182-8 |doi-access=free |issn=0894-0347}}</ref>.

The algebra <math>R_V := V/C_2(V)</math> with multiplication <math>a\cdot b = a_{-1}b \mod C_2(V)</math> is called the ''C<sub>2</sub>-algebra'' of <math>V</math>.

==Main properties==

* The multiplication of the C<sub>2</sub>-algebra is commutative and the additional binary operation <math>\{a,b\} = a_{0}b\mod C_2(V)</math> is a [[Poisson bracket]] on <math>R_V</math>which gives the C<sub>2</sub>-algebra the structure of a [[Poisson algebra]].<ref name=":0" />
* (Zhu's ''C''<sub>2</sub>-cofiniteness condition) If  <math>R_V</math>is finite dimensional then <math>V</math> is said to be ''C<sub>2</sub>-cofinite.'' There are two main representation theoretic properties related to C<sub>2</sub>-cofiniteness. A vertex operator algebra <math>V</math> is ''rational'' if the category of admissible modules is semisimple and there are only finitely many irreducibles. It was conjectured that rationality is equivalent to C<sub>2</sub>-cofiniteness and a stronger condition ''regularity,'' however this was disproved in 2007 by Adamovic and Milas who showed that the triplet vertex operator algebra is C<sub>2</sub>-cofinite but not rational''.'' <ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Li |first=Haisheng |date=1999 |title=Some Finiteness Properties of Regular Vertex Operator Algebras |journal=Journal of Algebra |volume=212 |issue=2 |pages=495–514 |doi=10.1006/jabr.1998.7654 |doi-access=free |s2cid=16072357 |issn=0021-8693|arxiv=math/9807077 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dong |first1=Chongying |last2=Li |first2=Haisheng |last3=Mason |first3=Geoffrey |date=1997 |title=Regularity of Rational Vertex Operator Algebras |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=132 |issue=1 |pages=148–166 |doi=10.1006/aima.1997.1681 |doi-access=free |s2cid=14942843 |issn=0001-8708|arxiv=q-alg/9508018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Adamović |first1=Dražen |last2=Milas |first2=Antun |date=2008-04-01 |title=On the triplet vertex algebra W(p) |journal=Advances in Mathematics |volume=217 |issue=6 |pages=2664–2699 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2007.11.012 |issn=0001-8708|doi-access=free }}</ref> Various weaker versions of this conjecture are known, including that regularity implies C<sub>2</sub>-cofiniteness<ref name=":1" /> and that for C<sub>2</sub>-cofinite <math>V</math> the conditions of rationality and regularity are equivalent.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Abe |first1=Toshiyuki |last2=Buhl |first2=Geoffrey |last3=Dong |first3=Chongying |date=2003-12-15 |title=Rationality, regularity, and 𝐶₂-cofiniteness |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=356 |issue=8 |pages=3391–3402 |doi=10.1090/s0002-9947-03-03413-5 |doi-access=free |issn=0002-9947}}</ref> This conjecture is a vertex algebras analogue of [[Cartan's criterion#Cartan's criterion for semisimplicity|Cartan's criterion]] for [[Semisimple Lie algebra|semisimplicity]] in the theory of [[Lie algebra|Lie algebras]] because it relates a structural property of the algebra to the semisimplicity of its representation [[Category (mathematics)|category]]. 
* The grading on <math>V</math> induces a filtration <math>A(V) = \bigcup_{p \ge 0} A_p(V)</math> where <math>A_p(V) = \operatorname{im}(\oplus_{j = 0}^p V_p\to A(V))</math> so that <math>A_p(V) \ast A_q(V) \subset A_{p+q}(V).</math> There is a surjective morphism of Poisson algebras <math>R_V \to \operatorname{gr}(A(V))</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arakawa |first1=Tomoyuki |last2=Lam |first2=Ching Hung |last3=Yamada |first3=Hiromichi |date=2014 |title=Zhu's algebra, C2-algebra and C2-cofiniteness of parafermion vertex operator algebras |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=264 |pages=261–295 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2014.07.021 |s2cid=119121685 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708}}</ref>

==Associated variety==

Because the C<sub>2</sub>-algebra <math>R_V</math> is a [[commutative algebra]] it may be studied using the language of [[algebraic geometry]]. The ''associated scheme'' <math>\widetilde{X}_V</math> and ''associated variety'' <math>X_V</math> of <math>V</math> are defined to be <math display="block">\widetilde{X}_V := \operatorname{Spec}(R_V)</math>, <math display="block">X_V := (\widetilde{X}_V)_{\mathrm{red}}</math> which are an [[affine scheme]] and an  [[Affine variety|affine algebraic variety]] respectively. <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Arakawa |first=Tomoyuki |date=2010-11-20 |title=A remark on the C 2-cofiniteness condition on vertex algebras |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/s00209-010-0812-4 |journal=Mathematische Zeitschrift |volume=270 |issue=1–2 |pages=559–575 |doi=10.1007/s00209-010-0812-4 |s2cid=253711685 |issn=0025-5874|arxiv=1004.1492 }}</ref> Moreover, since <math>L(-1)</math> acts as a derivation on <math>R_V</math><ref name=":0" /> there is an [[Group action|action]] of <math>\mathbb{C}^\ast</math> on the associated scheme making ''<math>\widetilde{X}_V</math>'' a [[Cone (algebraic geometry)|conical]] Poisson scheme and <math>X_V</math> a conical Poisson variety. In this language, C<sub>2</sub>-cofiniteness is equivalent to the property that <math>X_V</math> is a point.

'''Example:'''  If <math>W^k(\widehat{\mathfrak g}, f)</math> is the affine [[W-algebra]] associated to [[affine Lie algebra]] <math>\widehat{\mathfrak g}</math> at level <math>k</math> and nilpotent element <math>f</math> then <math>\widetilde{X}_{W^k(\widehat{\mathfrak g}, f)} = \mathcal{S}_f</math>is the [[Nilpotent orbit|Slodowy slice]] through <math>f</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Arakawa |first=T. |date=2015-02-19 |title=Associated Varieties of Modules Over Kac-Moody Algebras and C2-Cofiniteness of W-Algebras |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnu277 |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnu277 |issn=1073-7928|arxiv=1004.1554 }}</ref>
